body:
Account summary
- AcmeAI evaluating Redwood Dedicated for production support-agent workload. Primary driver: predictable latency + cost controls, plus safe rollouts (canaries/fallback already in use).
- New: strong interest in Console route-level A/B testing + eval reporting as a paid add-on (they want to standardize experiments across teams; currently doing ad-hoc comparisons).

Customer stakeholders (AcmeAI)
- Priya S. (Director of ML Platform) – owns inference vendor selection + rollout tooling.
- Daniel K. (SRE Manager) – wants guardrails/auto-rollback + incident playbooks.
- Morgan L. (Security/Compliance) – audit logs, retention policy, export to SIEM.
- Jenna R. (PM, Support AI) – cares about “quality delta” story and how to interpret results.

Redwood stakeholders
- AE: Alex Romero
- SE: Simran Kaur
- Product: Marissa Cole (Console & Rollouts)
- Telemetry/analytics: Logan Wright (instrumentation expectations)
- SRE (guardrails): Sean Gallagher (minimum bar for beta)
- Evals: Jonas Weber / Olivia Grant (offline suite attachment scope)

What they asked for (A/B + eval reporting add-on)
- Route-level traffic splits at /v1/chat/completions for specific projects (start with 90/10 then 50/50).
- Deterministic assignment (stickiness) so they can debug regressions; asked if it can key on a stable user identifier header.
- Reporting must include: p50/p95/p99 latency, TTFT, token usage, per-request cost attribution, error/timeout rates.
- Quality: wants offline eval suite attachment and a simple “quality delta” view (control vs variant), with confidence indicators + warnings on low sample sizes.
- Auditability: needs who/when changed experiment config, start/stop/rollback events, and export-friendly logs.
- Guardrails: “If p95 goes +15% or error rate spikes, we need the platform to scream and ideally roll back.” (their words)

Packaging / pricing notes (not finalized)
- They explicitly framed this as an add-on to Dedicated: willing to pay for (1) experimentation + results reporting and (2) eval reporting tied to experiments.
- Asked whether add-on pricing is per-seat vs per-experiment vs usage-based. Preference: per workspace/project (predictable for procurement).
- They want beta access regardless of final pricing, but need a draft to socialize internally by late March.

Timeline / activity log
- 2026-02-12: Internal Redwood sync (AE/SE + Marissa) — confirm AcmeAI as top beta candidate; requested we share constraints upfront (no bandits, limited custom metrics).
- 2026-02-17: Architecture review notes shared internally (exposure logging + privacy/retention questions raised by AcmeAI security).
- 2026-03-05: Beta partner call (Fireflies: 2026-03-05-ab-testing-beta-partner-sync-acmeai) — they agreed to start with 10% traffic in us-east, single route, 2 variants (same base model, different quantization + runtime settings).
- 2026-03-07: Follow-up email: AcmeAI asked for (a) sample audit log event payloads, (b) metric definitions for TTFT vs end-to-end, (c) retention defaults for exposure logs and whether they can be shortened.

POC proposal (beta)
- Scope: 1 project, 1 route, 2 variants, start at 90/10 for 48h, then 50/50 for 5–7 days if guardrails clean.
- Success criteria:
  - No >10% p95 latency regression (week-over-week baseline) and no sustained error-rate increase.
  - Cost per 1k tokens down 10–15% on variant B, or equivalent latency improvement.
  - Offline eval suite shows no statistically meaningful quality drop (or acceptable trade-off documented by PM).

Key risks called out
- Metric mismatch risk: they’ve previously had discrepancies between vendor consoles and internal dashboards; they asked for clear definitions + ability to export raw aggregates.
- Security sensitivity around “exposure logs” (they want assurance no prompt/user PII is stored in experiment events; only IDs/hashes).

Next steps (next 2 weeks)
1) Redwood to send: add-on packaging strawman + beta terms (Alex/Marissa) by 2026-03-13.
2) Simran to provide: ‘how stickiness works’ explanation and required headers for stable assignment; include troubleshooting for variant flipping.
3) Kick off security review: audit log coverage, retention controls, export to SIEM (Morgan L. + Redwood security consult) — target start 2026-03-18.
4) Confirm the exact eval suite/prompt set they’ll use; Jonas/Olivia to sanity check sample size guidance and how results will be presented in Console.

Open questions
- Do they require EU data residency for this workload in 2026H2? Mentioned possible expansion to eu-west if initial rollout works.
- Are they okay with Dedicated-only beta (Private later)? They said yes for now, but procurement may ask about longer-term on-prem option.
